Having lived in Colorado, I had a picture of what this was in my head before clicking the link.

Fun fact time:

Colorado is divided pretty nicely vertically into three distinct geographical areas.

  • To the east is the plains section. This is extremely flat, full of grass and groundhogs, and looks a lot like the plains that fill the states to the east of CO

  • In the center is the mountains section. The rocky mountains begin on both sides with foothills and are fairly wide. This part is my favorite.

  • To the west is the desert section. This is MUCH drier than the plains section and is full of plateaus and shrub-steppes like in the link.
That is interesting! Is there any particular reason why the central section is your favorite?

TONS of places where you can hike and go see some amazing sights.

During the winter, some of the best skiing/snowboarding in the country, my favorite being Vail

It's home to some of the highest mountains in the contiguous United States
